SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - MARCH 1, 2021 - 02:00 P.M.
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 818 0931 1722
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
* THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER REMAINS CLOSED TO THE PUBLIC*
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN THIS MEETING ARE LISTED BELOW
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber remains closed to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting using any of the following methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 10:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 10:00 a.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81809311722
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 818 0931 1722
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL HELD MARCH 1,
2021, 2:00 P.M., IN HYBRID MODE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA AND VIA TELECONFERENCE AS AUTHORIZED BY
STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 818 0931 1722

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 2:00 p.m.

2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council Member Bruce Barrows
  Council Member Grace Hu
  Council Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem Chuong Vo
  Mayor Naresh Solanki

4.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos Charter (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  A report was provided by Councilmember Barrows, who was authorized by the City
  Council to conduct a preliminary assessment of items which the City Council may want
  to consider during the comprehensive public review of the Cerritos City Charter.

  Pam Lee, Interim City Attorney, addressed items within the current City Charter which
  are currently in conflict with State, statutory, or case law, including the one-year
  eligibility period for elective office articulated in City Charter Section 401 and the public
  works contract bid thresholds in City Charter Section 905.

  Written correspondence
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Murali Vasudevan submitted written correspondence requesting future study sessions to
  be conducted at 7:00 p.m.

  The preamble and each Article of the Cerritos City Charter was reviewed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period as each Article of the City Charter was
  reviewed. Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence
  or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  Specific items which were highlighted for follow-up at future City Charter review study
  sessions included:

  1. Addressing current City Charter language which may conflict with State or current
  law (including Sections 401 – eligibility for elective office; Section 416 – ordinance
  violation; Section 905 – public works contracts bidding; Section 1103 - severability);

4.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos Charter (COUNCIL) (continued)

  2. Removal of gender-specific language and replacement with gender-neutral language
  (throughout the City Charter document);

  3. Addressing operational efficiency “clean-up” items, including:

  a. Council majority approval of waiver of reading in full for ordinances, rather than
  unanimous approval (Section 412);
  b. Setting penalties for ordinance violation by ordinance, rather than setting a
  specific amount which may not be in line with current practice in penalty
  provisions (Section 416);
  c. Increasing time period prior to the new fiscal year from thirty-five (35) to sixty
  (60) days for delivery of proposed budget to the City Council (Section 902);
  d. Setting the threshold for public works contracts to be bid by ordinance, rather
  than limiting the bid threshold amount to $7,500 (Section 905);
  e. Setting the threshold for violations of the City Charter by ordinance, rather than
  limiting to a specific dollar amount or length of time of imprisonment (Section
  1102);

  4. Addition of language in Section 404 that designates the Mayor as the City’s “official
  spokesperson” and also include a designee, if necessary;

  5. Addition of a “nepotism” policy to be placed in Article VI;

  6. Updating the purpose of the charter to reflect the change in the community’s
  character by removing language related to the agricultural industry (Section 1101);

  7. Review of City Charter Section 400, as related to term limits, will take place at a
  future City Charter review study session, as the matter may necessitate a dedicated
  study session meeting for comprehensive evaluation;

  8. Scheduling some of the future City Charter review study sessions in the evening and
  weekends in order to ensure broad community participation in the process.

5.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 3:04 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk
